title: Dynamic Object Model Emulation
pattern: Re-implementing polymorphic method dispatch by storing closures in a key-value hash map.
why_bad: It destroys compiler calling optimizations, prevents type-checking of parameter bounds, and causes runtime panics if a method lookup string is misspelled.
detection: The presence of structs that contain maps of function pointers or closures called via string lookups.
counterexample: `None`. Rust's native static or dynamic dispatch should always be preferred over manual maps of closures.
source: Benjamin C. Pierce - _Types and Programming Languages_ (2002, MIT).pdf, Chapter 18 "Imperative Objects".
